subject: flat-earthers
one_liner: Send money anywhere on the disc. Every payment travels in a straight line and stops well short of the ice wall.
brand_voice_notes: A payments company that is completely calm about geography everyone else got wrong. Compliance-memo tone. Treats the ice wall, the dome and line-of-sight as routine risk controls, the way a bank talks about fraud holds. Never mocks the customer, never winks. Numbers are precise. The word 'globe' is handled like a slur the legal team asked us to avoid.

hero.sub: Edgewise is the first payments network built on the map you already trust. No curvature fees. No routing through hemispheres. Every transfer is held a regulation 40 feet back from the ice wall.

features.title: Ice Wall Protection
features.blurb: Funds in transit are geofenced to stay inside the Antarctic perimeter. In eleven months of operation, zero dollars have gone over the edge. Our competitors will not publish that number.

features.title: Line-of-Sight Settlement
features.blurb: A payment settles when the recipient is visible from the sender's location with a reasonable telescope. If they are not, the transfer is flagged as a curvature claim and refunded within 3 to 5 business days.

features.title: One Flat Fee
features.blurb: Other apps charge for converting between hemispheres. We charge 1.9% per transfer, because there is only the one side and it is the top.

demo_screen_concept: A send-money dashboard laid over an azimuthal flat-disc map centered on the North Pole, ringed by a hatched ice wall. The user picks a recipient from a contact list; their pin lights up on the disc and a ruler-straight line is drawn from the sender in Ohio. A verification panel runs the line-of-sight check (telescope magnification, haze, 'distance to rim') and returns Settled, Held at Ice Wall, or Curvature Claim. A 'show conventional routing' toggle draws the dashed great-circle arc competitors use, labelled for comparison only. Tabs switch between Send, Activity (a ledger with statuses) and Wall Status (perimeter sectors with integrity readings).

design_direction.style: Engraved antique sea-chart fintech, parchment daylight mode. A modern payments product printed as a 16th-century copperplate map: aged parchment ground, navy engraving lines, a compass rose, rhumb lines radiating across sections, cartouche frames around headings, and an oxblood wax seal. Explicitly absent, because the last seven entries used them: acorn marks, dot maps, status-dot lists, terminal panels, name tags, punch cards, thermal tickets, matte dark mode, lime LEDs, conflict markers, gutter stripes, data strips, viewfinder brackets, infrared, thumbnail circles and arrows, VHS labels, OSD menus, tracking lines. Also absent: dark backgrounds, glassmorphism, neon, gradients behind text, sans-serif headlines. Four motifs carry the page. (1) The rhumb lines: thin navy hairlines at 8 percent radiate from a compass rose behind the hero and pricing. (2) The cartouche: section headings sit inside a double-ruled frame with small notched corners, like the title block of an old chart. (3) The scale bar: every section divider is an alternating ink and parchment map scale bar labelled in leagues. (4) The wax seal: oxblood #9E2B1F is rationed to the primary CTA, the highlighted tier and the Settled stamp, each shaped as a round seal. Corners 2px. Shadows are a single 1px ink hairline plus a 3px offset parchment-dark drop on cards.

fonts.display: 'IM Fell English', 'Iowan Old Style', Georgia, serif

design_direction.archetype: Fintech consumer app landing: hero with product promise, three feature cards, testimonials, three-tier pricing, then the demo CTA
design_direction.motion_vocab: Slow and surveyed. The compass rose needle settles with a single damped swing on load; rhumb lines draw in with stroke-dashoffset over 900ms; cards lift 2px on hover. Everything respects prefers-reduced-motion. No bounce, no parallax.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Two columns on desktop. Left: small-caps kicker 'Payments for the known world', the IM Fell h1 at clamp(44px, 6vw, 84px), the sub, the oxblood seal CTA and a ghost 'open the demo' link. Right: the engraved hero image in a double-ruled map frame with corner degree ticks, a compass rose overlapping its lower-left corner. Rhumb lines behind everything. Stacks to one column under 860px with the image first.

images.rationale: Engraved-chart direction calls for a hero illustration, so 1 hero (Flammarion-style engraving of a man at the rim of the disc). Demo is an SVG map, not photo-shaped, so no demo assets. Remaining 3 on testimonial headshots for the three named customers.

items.prompt: Antique copperplate engraving in the style of a 16th-century woodcut print: a lone traveller in a long coat kneels at the very rim of a flat world and pushes his head through the edge of the sky dome, looking out at the mechanism beyond. Calm sea and small hills behind him. Fine cross-hatched navy ink lines (#1E3A66) on aged warm parchment paper (#F2E8D2), subtle oxblood (#9E2B1F) tint only on the traveller's coat. One focal subject. Hand-engraved line art, museum print quality. No text, no letters, no numbers, no captions, no banners, no logos, no watermarks, no rendered UI screens.
